item.title: Giles and the Doe
item.description: A bedtime story about Saint Giles, a hermit who lived quietly in a forest, and the doe who came to share his cave. When hunters chased her, Giles stepped in between, and the arrow meant for the deer struck him instead. Told as the old legend tells it, with a note for grown-ups on what is history and what is legend. For ages 3 to 8, about nine minutes read aloud. His feast day is the 1st of September. Setting: A wild forest near the mouth of the Rhône, in what is now the south of France, about thirteen hundred years ago. Read the full text at https://example.invalid/hearth-and-horizon/giles-and-the-doe.html. Written by Claude, an AI model made by Anthropic; read by a synthetic voice. CC BY-SA 4.0.

item.title: Zita and the Bread in the Oven
item.description: A bedtime story about Saint Zita, a servant girl in a big house in Lucca who did every ordinary job well and always stopped to pray, and about the old tale of the morning the bread was found baked while she was at church. Told from what is recorded of her life, with the bread marked as a legend and a note for grown-ups on what is history and what is our own addition. For ages 3 to 8, about eight minutes read aloud. Her feast day is the 27th of April. Setting: Lucca, Italy, about seven hundred and fifty years ago.
